notes: Arizona's request_* figures are mail ballots issued (sent out), not applications received - this state's early voting is run through a permanent early-voting list rather than a one-off per-election request.
Some statistics provided by [PDI](https://politicaldata.com/). The higher value provided by the California Secretary of State or PDI is used where reporting differences exist.

Delaware does not publish mail ballot request data. The "ballots requested" figures shown for Delaware are the number of mail ballots received and counted, treated as equal to requests for lack of any other source.

The DC Board of Elections reports mail ballots returned in two separate files (drop box and USPS). There is no separate outstanding-request count, so request_all is set equal to the total returned. No party, age, or geographic breakdown is available. In-person early voting is not yet included; a third file covering it is expected later in the cycle.
Some Florida statistics are obtained from county websites that may report more recent and higher numbers than the Florida Division of Elections reports.

Georgia's county-level "Ballots Issued and Accepted" and "Ballots to Date" downloads (from the state's election-data-hub dashboard, https://sos.ga.gov/page/election-data-hub-unofficial-turnout) are compared against the statewide absentee file, county by county, using whichever is higher - this is how same-day in-person early-voting activity (which the statewide absentee file doesn't carry until the next overnight refresh) gets folded in. No district or demographic breakdown is available from these county-level downloads.

Idaho's daily absentee file covers mail ballots only - in-person early voting counts are scraped separately from the state's own dashboard (https://voteidaho.gov/data-and-dashboards/absentee-tracker/) and added in as a single statewide/county total, with no party, age, or gender breakdown available for it (the dashboard's own party breakdown mixes mail and in-person together, so it can't be used to split out the in-person-only portion). Congressional and state-legislative district totals are mail ballots only and do not include in-person early voting, so they will run lower than the statewide/county totals.

Iowa's BALLOT_STATUS field is not fully documented - this site infers whether a mail ballot was accepted from whether it has a RECEIVED_DATE rather than from BALLOT_STATUS directly. Figures may be revised once the Iowa Secretary of State's office provides official field documentation.

Kentucky reports are typically time-stamped one day behind when they are updated to this site. The reported date is as of the upload to this site is so that site vistors can be aware when a new report is available.
Louisiana does not publish mail ballot request data - the ballots requested figures shown for Louisiana equal ballots returned. Louisiana rreports statistics for Whites, Blacks, and other only.

Maryland reports are typically time-stamped one day behind when they are updated to this site. The reported date is as of the upload to this site is so that site vistors can be aware when a new report is available.

These statistics are compiled from an individual level file which may have slightly different statistics than the state's summary report. I believe the discrepancy is due to timing of when the state generates these data. The individual file has age and district identifiers that allow me to produce more statistics.
South Carolina's in-person early-voting total (by county) comes from a separate report with no race or Hispanic ethnicity breakdown; the race/ethnicity figures shown reflect mail ballots only.
Tennessee's daily turnout report provides a cumulative county-level total for in-person early voters only. No mail-ballot figures or demographic data are available for Tennessee at at this time.
Texas does not report mail ballot requests. Requests are equal to mail ballots sent.

Utah is a universal vote-by-mail state - every "Active" registered voter is automatically mailed a ballot each election, and a 2025 law phasing this out does not take effect until 2029. Statewide and county "ballots requested" figures are therefore the number of Active registered voters by party, scraped from the Lt. Governor's current voter registration statistics page. Congressional district figures instead use accepted ballots as a stand-in, since Utah does not publish district-level registration or request data.

notes: Washington is a universal vote-by-mail state - every active registered voter is automatically mailed a ballot, so the "ballots requested" figures shown are active registered voters (from the state's own voter registration file) rather than a separate request count. Gender is the only demographic breakdown available for Washington; no party, race, or age data is published with ballot returns.

West Virginia publishes in-person early vote returns by county and party only - there is no mail-ballot figure and no separate ballots-requested figure, so the "ballots requested" figures shown equal early vote returns. No age, gender, race, or district-level data is available.
